We just published a list of the 10 Stocks With Insane Upside According to Reddit and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) ranked 10th on this list.

US stocks edged lower Thursday, snapping a rebound that had lifted the S&P 500 1.3% a day earlier. The S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40, the Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped 0.36% to 52,297.09, and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.39% to 25,366.09, Yahoo Finance reported, as bond yields rose. Traders weighed hot inflation data, the Federal Reserve's next move and higher oil prices.

Photo by osamu nakazawa on Unsplash

Hot Inflation Keeps the Fed in Focus

The week's moves have been shaped by interest rates. Tuesday's hotter-than-expected inflation report convinced traders that the Federal Reserve will raise rates next month, Reuters said. According to CME FedWatch, investors fully price in a hike of at least 25 basis points, with a 13.2% chance of a 50-basis-point move. Several Fed officials have said they are open to a more aggressive path, and Wall Street analysts have raised their forecasts for more and bigger hikes, Yahoo Finance said.

Wednesday's rebound showed how quickly sentiment can swing. The S&P 500 gained 1.3% and the Nasdaq Composite 1.6% after results from an AI cloud company eased worries about the durability of the artificial intelligence trade, Reutersreported, with advancing stocks outnumbering decliners by 1.3 to 1 on the NYSE. The Treasury market was closed for Veterans Day, so bond traders could react only on Thursday.

Oil Adds to the Uncertainty

Thursday brought another pressure point. Oil prices climbed after the president said he was no longer interested in a deal with Iran, the Associated Press reported, which complicates the inflation outlook. Higher energy costs feed into the same inflation numbers the Fed is fighting. Even so, the S&P 500 finished with a modest loss and is up 2.9% for the week.

Retail investors are watching the same swings closely, and Reddit threads tend to cluster around names where the gap between price and analyst expectations looks widest. That gap deserves some care. An average price target is a twelve-month estimate pulled from sell-side analysts, it is often revised after earnings, and a handful of outliers can skew the mean. Because upside is measured against the current share price, a sharp drop widens it overnight, while a rally shrinks it just as fast. Readers who follow that chatter can browse our list of undervalued stocks to buy according to Reddit. You may also want to read our ranking of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts are spotting 50%-plus upside.

Wall Street's AI trade just had one of its worst weeks in years. Politics and inflation hit it at the same time. The Nasdaq Composite posted its deepest one-day drop since April 2025 last week, after Democrats swept the midterm elections and investors began weighing tougher scrutiny of AI and limits on data center construction. The Cboe Volatility Index climbed to a seven-month high the same day.

Why the AI Selloff Hit Chip and Data Center Stocks So Hard

Stocks first cheered the election. They closed sharply higher the day after the vote because the result cleared up political uncertainty. Then chipmakers and data center operators fell, even as the biggest, cash-rich AI spenders rose. A slower buildout eases cash demands on the companies doing the spending, but it squeezes the operators and suppliers whose growth depends on fast construction.

Scott Chronert, head of US equity strategy at Citi Research, said a change in the pace of the data center buildout changes the basic path for many of those suppliers. Our list of oversold AI stocks where Wall Street analysts see 50% upside or more covers more of the group.

Hot Inflation Puts the Fed Back in Focus

Inflation added a second worry. The Labor Department said consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, a third straight gain of 0.4% or more. Economists polled by Reuters had expected 0.3%. Markets now fully price in a Federal Reserve rate increase of at least 25 basis points in December, up from 84% a day earlier, according to CME FedWatch.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the central bank should raise rates in December even if inflation had cooled. He said a half-point move should be considered if the picture worsened. Jason Ware, chief investment officer at Albion Financial Group, said investors began to wonder whether the Fed worried more about inflation than they did, and sold some stocks.

The rout wiped out trillions of dollars in market value and clouded the outlook for a global economy the AI boom has been supporting. Readers following the chip side of the trade can find more names in our list of the best semiconductor stocks to buy for the next decade. Ahead of the Fed's December meeting, traders expect about two more quarter-point increases in total this cycle, according to LSEG data.

Advanced Micro Devices' (AMD) stock looks poised to revisit its all-time highs. The market has already bought into its growth story. Now, the next opportunity may lie in how much of that growth turns into profits. After a triple-digit gain in 2026, the stock has pulled back from its October record highs, but the fundamentals help explain much of that rally.

In its third-quarter earnings report, released on November 3, the Santa Clara, California-based chipmaker reported that its Data Center revenue nearly doubled, along with a great improvement in margins.

The most interesting part may still be ahead. With much greater visibility into 2027, I believe the market still underestimates the company's earnings growth potential. That's why I remain bullish, even with an already demanding valuation.

AMD's Data Center Growth Explains Much of the Rally

First, I think it's important to put AMD's remarkable triple-digit rally this year into context. I see two key metrics that have marked a turning point in the company's investment thesis: Data Center revenue growth and forward revenue growth.

Let's start by breaking down the first metric. Basically, the market has gone from viewing AMD as a central processing unit (CPU) manufacturer trying to gain ground in artificial intelligence (AI) graphics processing units (GPUs) to treating it as a potential second major AI infrastructure platform, behind Nvidia (NVDA).

The acceleration driven by AI demand really began to show up in AMD's results in 2026, something that wasn't nearly as pronounced in 2025. To be more specific, in the third quarter of 2025, AMD generated $4.34 billion in Data Center revenue, up 22% year-over-year. A year later, that revenue reached $8.55 billion, a 97% jump, driven by both EPYC processors, benefiting particularly from the growth of AI agents, and Instinct MI450 GPUs. As a result, Data Center now accounts for 64% of the company's total revenue, compared to less than 50% in the same period last year.

As if that weren't enough, this growth came with a considerable improvement in the segment's profitability. Data Center's operating margin rose from 25% to 34%. So, we're talking about a company whose core business has nearly doubled in size while its margins have expanded by an impressive 9 percentage points.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE) has fallen about 15% in three months, but HSBC sees room for a rebound as AI data centers look for power they can generate on-site. Analyst Samantha Hoh put Bloom on the bank's buy list with a $350 price target, about 73% above Thursday's $201.93 close. The call hinges on whether Bloom can turn demand for its fuel cells into cash as it expands production.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Signs with BE.

Is BE fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

BE GF Value chart

Bloom sells, installs and services solid oxide fuel cell systems that generate electricity at customer sites. Its customers include data center operators, utilities and industrial businesses. On-site generation can help data centers start operating sooner in markets where grid connections take longer.

Hoh pointed to Bloom's profitable service business and nearly 3 gigawatts of installed capacity. The company's Nov. 5 agreement with NTT Data covers 900 megawatts across multiple data center projects. Oracle also says Bloom remains the primary power supplier for its Project Jupiter campus in New Mexico following reports of delays.

Bloom's third-quarter revenue rose 138% to $1.24 billion, and the company lifted its 2026 sales outlook to $4.4 billion$4.6 billion. Still, it used $27.1 million in operating cash and spent $153.5 million on property and equipment, leaving free cash flow about $181 million negative.

Investors Takeaway

The next earnings report will show whether customer payments are keeping pace with spending on factory capacity. Watch operating cash flow, capital expenditures and whether adjusted gross margin holds near the company's full-year outlook of 34%.

Installation milestones at Oracle and NTT Data could clarify when those agreements will translate into revenue. On-time deployments and improving cash flow would strengthen HSBC's case. Factory cost overruns or further project delays could keep cash under pressure even if sales continue to climb.

Key Takeaways

Bloom Energy rose 13% in the past week, with Vertiv and Oracle, after CoreWeave and Constellation Energy raised their 2026 guidance.

Bloom had no news of its own, and with its orders and rising estimates intact, the bounce looks like it has further to go.

The stock trades well below its usual forward P/E, though negative free cash flow is the risk to watch.

Bloom Energy (BE:NYSE) is up 13% in the past week with no news of its own. AI power stocks sank after the midterms, and investors came back once CoreWeave (CRWV:NASDAQ) and Constellation Energy showed the data-center buildout is still on.

Vertiv (VRT:NYSE) rose on the same relief, as did Oracle (ORCL:NYSE), the customer behind Bloom's biggest order.

The buildout is still on

Constellation beat estimates and raised its 2026 guidance before Monday's open, easing fears for power suppliers. That day, RBC Capital analyst Chris Dendrinos kept his Outperform rating and $335 target on Bloom: "We do not think datacenters are dead."

After Tuesday's close, CoreWeave beat estimates and raised its 2026 revenue guidance to a range of $13.0 billion to $13.3 billion. It also raised the low end of its 2026 capital spending range to $37 billion, keeping the top at $39 billion. Bloom was among the power stocks that rallied on the news.

That spending reaches Vertiv too, up 14% in the past week. On Oct. 28, it reported third-quarter net sales up 61% to $4.31 billion, with organic orders more than doubling, and raised its 2026 guidance. Its next report, early next year, will show whether budgets like CoreWeave's keep those orders climbing.

Bloom's orders never went away

Bloom's customers kept signing. NTT DATA agreed on Nov. 5 to 900 megawatts of its on-site power, on top of Oracle's 2.8-gigawatt deal. Oracle, up 7% in the past week, is the one to watch: its data-center build left it with negative free cash flow of $5 billion in the three months to Aug. 31, and its mid-December report will show whether it's keeping that pace.

Analysts kept raising estimates, too. Consensus normalized EPS for 2027 rose to $5.32 from $4.88 in the 30 days to Nov. 10. Meanwhile, 2028's $8.24 is more than 10 times 2025's $0.76:
